evals.name: collapsed-tile-badge
offscreen-clone-context
evals.prompt: I'm building virtualization for a feed. Before rendering a row I need its height so I can position rows. My approach: I clone the row node and append the clone to document.body with `position:absolute; visibility:hidden; height:auto`, then read `getBoundingClientRect().height`. It mostly works, but a bunch of rows come back noticeably shorter than they actually render, and rows in our themed "compact density" mode are especially wrong. The real rows live inside a container that uses container queries and CSS custom properties for spacing and font size. What's going wrong, and what should I do instead?

evals.name: animate-to-content-height
evals.prompt: Write a React + TypeScript hook `useAutoHeight` for an expand/collapse panel: when open, the container animates its height from 0 to the natural height of its children, and back to 0 when closed. It needs to handle children whose height can change while open (text that reflows on resize, async content that loads in later). Give me the hook plus the minimal CSS. Keep it robust — I've been bitten before by the height being measured wrong.
